newsitem.title: SPAIN: FOCUS - BBV 96 earnings up as core business solid.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - BBV 96 earnings up as core business solid.

text.p: Spain's Banco Bilbao Vizcaya reported a jump of 24 percent in 1996 earnings on Thursday, displaying key strength in the hotly contested traditional banking business of loans, deposits and commissions.
Net attributable earnings rose to 104.26 billion pesetas ($759 million) from 84.01 billion, in line with expectations.
Net interest income, which reflects interest income from deposits and loans, jumped to 415.57 billion pesetas, compared with 343.27 billion a year earlier.
Ordinary profit, which covers commissions for bank services, increased to 586.87 billion in 1996 from 474.57 a year earlier.
Given the earnings rise, the bank raised its final dividend payout of the the year to 89 pesetas a share from 72 in 1995, and increased the total 1996 dividend to 230 pesetas from 198.
Chairman Emilio Ybarra, presenting the results to journalists, pointed to the strong rise in net interest income despite the "difficult environment" of interest rates.
Official money market interest rates fell 2.75 points last year, putting pressure on bank profit margins in loans and deposits amid heavy competition.
Bank analysts said BBV's results were as expected, but they were pleased at the strength in traditional business.
"These (results) are spectacular, and I would highlight above all the quality of the figures with strength in the recurrent earnings line," said a dealer at a Spanish bank.
To cope with the declining margins, many banks are expanding abroad and reaching out to new, more volatile sources of income - such as increased own-account trading.
BBV too has spread its wings, with an increase of 247.5 percent to 37.79 billion pesetas in financial trading and a portfolio of industrial holdings that earned a return on equity of 20 percent.
"These are good results in and of themselves. There is across-the-board improvement," said Juan de Dios Sanchez, banking analyst at Ahorro Corporacion in Madrid.
The strength in core lending and deposits suggests BBV is well-placed to benefit from the economic upswing and from rising consumer spending forecast for the year.
"If there is a pick-up in the economy, it's clear that BBV of all the banks stands to benefit the most," a trader at a foreign brokerage said.
Flush with success, BBV could not resist a swipe at leading Spanish bank Santander, whose earnings rose to a smaller 85.60 billion pesetas despite its larger assets.
"BBV has shown itself to be the better manager because with fewer assets than Spain's largest bank, it has obtained greater earnings," Ybarra told journalists.

Santander, which in 1993 humiliated then market-leader BBV by winning the bid for a controlling stake in Banesto, on Tuesday reported a 13.5 percent rise in attributable earnings. These results were in line with expectations. ($1=137.3 Peseta)
